_status: APPROVED: the local four (7 Nov) and three databases (9 Nov); the network four remain a proposal

_decisions._what: Calls that were the user's to make, recorded here rather than left in a chat log.

run_scope.note: The approved four are local: no network, no credentials. The other four send real traffic to someone else's service when their tools are called, so they stay unapproved and `eval real` does not include them in its default set.

label.decision: Leave every label null and state it as a limitation.
label.consequence: Gap 3's false-alarm rate is reported UNLABELLED. The measurement stands - an alarm on an upgrade where nothing malicious happened is a false alarm either way - but the benign versus benign-security-relevant split is not available, so no claim is made about whether the detector is noisier on security-relevant upgrades than on ordinary ones. This must appear in the write-up's limitations, not be quietly omitted.
label.why_not_assigned: The label is a reading of intent out of each changelog. Assigning it from a package summary would be asserting something about eight changelogs nobody read closely, and it is the label the rate is measured against.

rq3b_scope.conditions: mcp-server-motherduck in local DuckDB mode only, never its cloud mode; all three against throwaway database files.
rq3b_scope.consequence: RQ3b has 7 real servers (4 + 3), short of the 15 H3 asks for. Per GAPS_PLAN_v2's own fallback, RQ3b is reported on the approved servers and the shortfall is stated in the report's limitations; the false-alarm rate carries a wide interval and is not claimed to generalise.

_what_this_is: Candidate real MCP servers for Gap 3: the false-alarm rate of a
behavioural detector across genuine version upgrades.
All are real packages on PyPI with multiple published releases. Version
pairs, release dates and licences were read from the PyPI JSON API on
Two fields are NOT facts and are marked so on every entry:
label           benign or benign-security-relevant. This is a reading
of intent from a changelog and it is the label the
false-alarm rate is measured against, so it is the
user's call, not mine. Every entry has it null.
read_only_tools My guess from each package summary. A tool list cannot
be confirmed without starting the server and calling
tools/list, which needs the permission noted below.
Probing a tool that turns out to write would be a real
side effect on the machine, so these must be confirmed

_blocked_on.permission: Installing and running these requires executing third-party code from PyPI. Auto mode refused it as 'Code from External', which is the correct default: Gap 3 means downloading and running roughly twenty unknown MCP servers.
_blocked_on.needed: Explicit approval to pip-install pinned versions into throwaway virtual environments and start each server over stdio.
_blocked_on.scope_if_granted: Install only; no network egress beyond PyPI except where a server's own tools reach out, which is why the network-touching candidates are separated below.

_safety_notes.probe_values_are_harmless: The keyed generator emits .invalid hostnames and loopback port 9 (RFC 863 discard), and relative paths only. A fetch server probed this way attempts a request that cannot leave the machine.
_safety_notes.but_some_servers_reach_out: arxiv and duckduckgo servers send real queries to third-party services when called. The queries are benign, but that is outbound traffic to someone else's infrastructure and should be a deliberate choice rather than a side effect.
_safety_notes.recommended_first_set: time, calculator, git, sqlite. Purely local, no network, no credentials - enough to prove the pipeline before anything reaches outward.

servers.name: mcp-server-time
servers.why_shortlisted: Official Anthropic server. Pure computation, no network, no credentials. The safest thing to prove the pipeline on.

servers.name: mcp-server-calculator
servers.why_shortlisted: A minor-to-minor jump across a version boundary, so behaviour plausibly moved. Deterministic output, which makes any drift unambiguous.

servers.name: mcp-server-git
servers.why_shortlisted: Official. Has a clear read/write split, so the read-only subset is meaningful rather than nominal. Needs a throwaway repository to point at.
servers.caution: git_add, git_commit and git_reset must never be probed. Confirm the tool list before running.

servers.name: mcp-server-sqlite
entry: import sys; from mcp_server_sqlite import main; sys.exit(main())
servers.why_shortlisted: Crosses a versioning-scheme change (0.6.2 to a date-based scheme), which is exactly the kind of release where behaviour moves.
servers.caution: write_query and create_table exist. Point it at a throwaway database.
servers.entry_note: Neither 0.6.2 nor 2025.4.25 ships a __main__ module, so `-m mcp_server_sqlite` never started either release; both declare the console script mcp-server-sqlite = mcp_server_sqlite:main, which this calls. Found 15 Nov 2026 (H3b amendment 2).

servers.name: mcp-server-fetch
servers.why_shortlisted: Official, and the only shortlisted server whose whole purpose is network access - which makes it the interesting case for the side-effect rules.
servers.caution: Probes carry loopback and .invalid targets, so requests cannot leave the machine. Worth confirming that in the first run rather than trusting it.

servers.name: mcp-simple-arxiv
servers.why_shortlisted: Third-party rather than official, which matters for external validity - the gap is about the ecosystem, not about Anthropic's own code.
servers.caution: Sends real queries to arXiv. Benign, but it is someone else's service and should be a deliberate choice.

servers.name: duckduckgo-mcp-server
servers.why_shortlisted: Third-party, genuinely non-deterministic output - search results change - which is the hard false-alarm case for a behavioural detector.

servers.name: arxiv-mcp-server
servers.why_shortlisted: 41 releases, so upgrade pairs are plentiful and a patch-level pair is available - useful for showing a small upgrade is not automatically quiet.
servers.caution: download_paper writes files. Must not be probed.

servers.name: mcp-server-duckdb
entry: import sys; from mcp_server_duckdb import main; sys.exit(main())
servers.why_shortlisted: Local DuckDB file, opened --readonly so probes cannot change it.

servers.name: mcp-server-motherduck
servers.why_shortlisted: Local DuckDB mode only: --db-path is a local file, so the MotherDuck cloud is never contacted. Read-only by default for local files; --home-dir keeps DuckDB out of the user's real home.

servers.name: mcp-alchemy
servers.why_shortlisted: SQLAlchemy over a throwaway SQLite file, given through DB_URL.

excluded.name: mcp-server-sentry
excluded.reason: Needs a Sentry auth token. The plan excludes servers requiring paid or account-bound credentials, and a probe against someone's issue tracker is not a harmless call.

excluded.name: mcp-server-docker
excluded.reason: Requires a Docker daemon and its tools act on containers. Side effects are real and not confinable to a sandbox directory.

excluded.name: mcp-server-weather
excluded.reason: Only 5 releases and the package metadata did not parse cleanly. Revisit if more servers are needed.

excluded.name: Node-based servers
excluded.reason: Node.js is not installed on this machine, and the plan notes the sandbox monitor sees Python processes fully but Node only roughly - so their side-effect signals would not be comparable.

_shortfall.note: Eight is short of the target. Python MCP servers with two or more published releases are scarcer than the plan assumed - a search of the obvious candidates found eleven, and three were excluded for credentials or tooling. Reaching fifteen would mean either installing Node.js to take in the npm ecosystem, or relaxing to servers with only two releases. Both are decisions for the user, and the shortfall should be stated in the write-up rather than quietly met by padding the list.

_candidates._status: T29 candidates - NOT APPROVED. Read from the PyPI JSON API on 2026-11-09; nothing installed or run.
_candidates._why: H3 needs at least 15 real upgrades for a credible false-alarm rate; 4 servers are approved.
_unknowns: tools_changed is null on every entry: whether tools/list differs between the two releases can only be seen by installing both, which needs approval. A pair whose definitions did not change still counts (its residue is ordinary drift), as the plan allows.
entry is null: the launch arguments (a database path, a working directory) are read from each package's --help after approval, not guessed.
Licences marked '?' on PyPI must be confirmed before the package is cited.
